title: KaiserStillen - A prospective investigation of the impact of BFHI-based interventions on breastfeeding rate, breastfeeding self-efficacy, and attitudes toward breastfeeding after primary cesarean section.
summary: This study investigates whether specific support measures in the hospital – such as close physical contact between mother and child immediately after cesarean delivery, personalized breastfeeding counseling, and targeted preparation for the postpartum period – can make breastfeeding easier. The background is that many mothers experience difficulties with breastfeeding after cesarean birth. The study aims to find out whether additional support helps mothers feel more confident and breastfeed for a longer time. Adult women who plan to breastfeed their babies after a scheduled cesarean section can participate. The goal is to determine whether these supportive measures improve breastfeeding success and strengthen mothers’ confidence in their ability to breastfeed.
conditions: Other and unspecified disorders of lactation

interventions.name: Intervention group (BFHI-oriented measures: early and daily skin-to-skin contact, structured breastfeeding counseling, teaching videos, discharge planning).
Control group (standard care without additional interventions)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult women (≥ 18 years of age)
Planned delivery via primary / elective cesarean section at ≥ 37+0 weeks of gestation
Singleton pregnancy with physiological course
Healthy mother and healthy newborn without postpartum complications
Intention to breastfeed
Sufficient knowledge of German to participate in counseling
Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Multiple pregnancy
Preterm birth (< 37+0 weeks of gestation)
Serious maternal or neonatal pre-existing medical conditions
Postpartum admission of mother or newborn to intensive care
Medical contraindication to breastfeeding
Insufficient German language skills
No planned cesarean section
